title: Choose DataBridge's visual world
question: The roll assigned Wayfinding Signage. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Wayfinding Signage
options.lineage: Airport and rail wayfinding programs (Schiphol, Swiss and Dutch transit)
options.thesis: Every screen tells you, like an airport sign, where your data is coming from and where it is going.
materials: humanist signage sans with tabular figures
options.viewport: A yellow route sign spans the top: SOURCE server/database → TARGET server/database at sign scale; object tree with difference counts left, diff grid centre, SQL and risk pane right. Sign yellow is reserved for identity and direction; selection, focus and primary buttons use the OS accent colour.
options.risk: Yellow at sign scale can tire the eye in dark theme if it spreads past the route sign.

raised.raise: Type steps on one fixed scale (11/13/15/20/28); nothing is set between steps.
Difference counts share one fixed magnitude ramp, from tree rows to the summary.
One visible 8px armature: grid columns, pane edges and sign panels snap to the same cells.
Elevation has one rank: only overlays lift; state changes step instantly, no decorative easing.

options.label: Interlocking Route
options.thesis: A sync plan is a route: set it, lock it, then clear it, like a signal box.
options.viewport: The plan's dependency graph drawn as a track diagram; the approved route lights and locks, with the target as the terminal station.
options.risk: Familiar dark dev-tool look, and the diagram can tip into a control-panel costume.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: The plan is a coupon book: every operation is a coupon that is validated, used or voided, and nothing disappears.
options.viewport: Plan operations as tabbed coupons in dependency order; the execution manifest stamps each one.
options.case: Holds product clarity: coupons map exactly to the execution manifest. Loses audience identification: DBAs don't read travel stationery.
options.risk: Coupon framing gets heavy across a 10,000-row data diff.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Operations run like departures: fixed columns, live rows, and states that restyle a row without breaking the board.
options.viewport: The execution monitor as a board: operation, object, rows, status; failed rows drop to dim red.
options.case: Holds product clarity for execution and progress. Weaker on audience identification for schema diffs and SQL review.
options.risk: Strong on one screen, thin on the other nine.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Loses both axes: novelty type fights dense technical reading.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Magnitude as ranked dot size on a chart.
options.viewport: Objects plotted as stars by difference count.
options.case: Loses both axes: database objects have no spatial position to chart.
options.kept: One fixed magnitude ramp for counts.
options.risk: Decorative chart with no real coordinates.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid type over a visible armature.
options.case: Loses both axes: poster typography has no job on a working screen.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.thesis: Acetate leaves over coloured divider boards.
options.case: Loses both axes: layered leaves obscure dense grids.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral Fluent-style database tool, executed impeccably.
materials: neutral greys with one blue accent
canonCard.viewport: Object tree, diff grid and SQL pane, like Redgate SQL Compare or Visual Studio Schema Compare.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
